claims.claim: Semantic entropy and mutual information with embedding or CodeBLEU clustering, and token log-probabilities, do not significantly correlate with code correctness on LiveCodeBench.
claims.stance_target: L1: negative result for transferred NLG UQ on code
claims.quoted_support: Abstract: state-of-the-art techniques [27, 14, 3] fail to exhibit a correlation between estimated uncertainty and correctness when applied to code.

claims.claim: Symbolic-execution clustering restores significant correlation, and uniform-distribution estimates perform comparably, so token probabilities are not essential.
claims.quoted_support: Abstract: We further show that token-level probabilities are not essential - uncertainty estimates assuming uniform distributions perform comparably.

claims.claim: Symbolic cluster count used as an abstention threshold achieves a false positive rate below 0.02%.
claims.stance_target: L3: abstention with a sampled signal on code is OCCUPIED (abstention, not execution-budget routing)
claims.quoted_support: Abstract: it correlates with correctness and supports highly effective abstention policies, achieving a false positive rate below 0.02%.

breadth.confidence_families: semantic entropy, mutual information, LLM-Probability, symbolic cluster count (Abstract, Table 2)
breadth.reasoning_models: DeepSeek-R1 included; reasoning-on status not isolated
breadth.label_independence: tests independent of the symbolic executor
breadth.contamination_split: LiveCodeBench described as contamination-free; no date split stated
breadth.calibration_metrics: Pearson correlation and p-value (Table 2); FPR/FNR for abstention
